chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Minqari from Hisham al-Saydani who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hisham, if you see the two armies meet, do not neglect seeking sustenance on that day.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about seeking sustenance when two armies meet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Hisham al-Saydani to continue seeking sustenance (*rizq*) when the two armies meet, a phrase traditionally interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the battle of al-Hassan ibn Ali with Muawiya or, more eschatologically, the armies of the Mahdi. This guidance underscores the Shia principle that major historical or cosmic events do not negate the obligation of economic activity, but rather emphasize the need for material preparedness and stability amidst turmoil. It reflects the balance between spiritual awareness of divine signs and the practical duty of securing one's livelihood.
